decisions.reason: Session-log timeline connects the pwsh worker (child of the host) to the replaced tree; host dies first, GUI connection drops, result 'unknown by construction'; called a self-targeted kill, not flaky tool/network; no claim that every in-place upgrade on every platform crashes.

Content present but dsh.cmd missing + dsh.ps1 stale = command layer destroyed while tree half-built; hand-swap caused the non-standard state; explicitly 'never hand-copy package directories and never hand-write shims'.

Grounded in repair notes: external CLI, pinned rc.1 registry install regenerating all three shims, dsh --version=0.1.2-rc.1, source tag aligned with no unrelated edits; recorded repair vs left-to-user verification separated; no installs executed by the candidate.

Refusal/handoff and the stop→pinned-install→restart→refresh→verify procedure are fully correct (dependent tool shells/detached processes excluded), but the established-vs-new partition inverts the rubric: the self-host refusal is attributed to pre-existing R-12 and stop-host-first is listed as new.

Guard resolves own runtime identity (process.execPath/argv/module paths) and hard-denies self-targeting global mutations; zero-card corridor → no plugin re-migration; version markers + plugin fleet verified after restart/hard-refresh; backups removed only after confirmation; kept tag-specific.

caps.reason: Final advice: never execute from a session/tool call; fully stop every dsh process before the pinned external install.
Final fix is the formal pinned external install; manual directory swaps and handmade shims explicitly forbidden.
